info.bio:
Filter es una banda de metal industrial creada en 1993 por el ex guitarrista de Nine Inch Nails, Richard Patrick y Brian Liesegang. Su música actual es básicamente metal alternativo con leves tintes de electrónica. En sus inicios se sentía claramente la influencia de Nine Inch Nails, su sonido era mucho más oscuro y más orientado al rock industrial; pero con el tiempo se han alejado de esta tendencia apuntando más hacia el metal.

Liesegang abandonó Filter en 1997 argumentando diferencias creativas con Patrick.

scenes.name: La segunda venida del industrial
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: En los noventa el estilo brutal de Nine Inch Nails lo invade todo en EE UU y el industrial se vuelve fenómeno de masas; el «aggro» de KMFDM es menos visible pero igual de ubicuo: Grotus, Filter, Stabbing Westward, Acumen, Skrew, Electric Hellfire Club, Society Burning, Gravity Kills y, lo más original, Girls Vs Boys (Venus Luxure No.1 Baby) y New Wet Kojak. La EBM internacional se vuelve más brutal (Leaether Strip, Suicide Commando, :Wumpscut:, Hocico, Mentallo & The Fixer). La «música de la fábrica de la muerte» sobrevive en los escultores de ruido: los neozelandeses Dead C (Harsh '70s Reality, «música imposible de escuchar»), Gate, Bruce Russell, Namanax, Illusion Of Safety, Maeror Tri, Towering Inferno (Kaddish). Y el «digital hardcore» de Atari Teenage Riot y Alec Empire.

podcast.title: The Crow: City of Angels Soundtrack Contribution (1996)
podcast.body: Filter was featured on the soundtrack for *The Crow: City of Angels*, the 1996 sequel to *The Crow*. This collection was considered "pretty much as good as the first one" and included other prominent bands of the era. "Bush, Corn, Deftones, E-Pop, White Zombie, Filter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Crow: Salvation Soundtrack Contribution (2000)
podcast.body: Filter contributed to *The Crow: Salvation* soundtrack, released in the spring of 2000. This album was associated with the sequel to *The Crow: City of Angels*, although the movie itself did not appear until 2004 and went straight to DVD. "More Hole, More Filter, Monster Magnet, Stabbing Westward, Kid Rock, Crystal Method."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inspired by Skinny Puppy
podcast.body: Filter is explicitly listed as an artist who was inspired and influenced by the Canadian industrial band Skinny Puppy. "Here's a short list of artists who say they were inspired and influenced by Skinny Puppy, Ministry, Nine-inch Nails, Maryland Manson, the Prodigy, Ramstein, Filter, Corn, Lincoln Park, Evan Essence."

xref.title: Filter Records Dispute
xref.body: An issue arose concerning Filter Records, the label founded by Mark Hoppas's boss with his savings, leading to a legal dispute over the ownership rights of the early demo tapes that were released through the label. "Now that would later be an issue when there was a dispute over who actually owned these tapes."
